# Learn Basic Phrases in a New Language Using Alexa+'s AI Conversation Mode

**Hook:** By the end of this guide, you'll be able to ask your Amazon Echo device for a simple phrase in another language, hear it spoken aloud, and practise it back — all hands-free, with no typing needed. This is for complete beginners who want a low-pressure way to start learning a new language at home.

## Before you start
- An **Amazon Echo device** (such as an Echo Dot or Echo Show) that's already set up and connected to Wi-Fi.
- The **Alexa+** (an AI-powered upgrade to the standard Alexa assistant) feature available on your device. If you're not sure whether you have it, just say "Alexa, are you the new Alexa?" and the assistant will tell you.
- A **language in mind** to practise. This guide uses **Spanish** as the example, but the same approach works for French, Italian, German, Japanese, and many others.
- Around **10 minutes** for your first practice session.
- A quiet room helps the microphone pick up your voice clearly.

## Step 1 — Wake Alexa+ and ask for a language lesson

Say the wake word out loud: **"Alexa, open Conversations"** or simply **"Alexa, let's learn Spanish"**. The light ring on top of your Echo device will turn blue and spin, which means Alexa+ is listening. If you've never used the new conversational mode before, Alexa+ may greet you and ask what you'd like to do. Speak one short request at a time, then pause for a second so it can hear you clearly. **If it looks different:** on Echo Show devices with a screen, you may see a panel called **"Conversations"** or **"AI Chat"** on the home screen — tap that to start. If your device only responds with the old-style Alexa, the Alexa+ feature may not yet be enabled on your account.
💬 Example: say *"Alexa, I want to practise Spanish."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ replies in a friendly voice and asks what level you're at, or simply starts the conversation.

## Step 2 — Choose a topic and set your level

Tell Alexa+ what you want to learn about — for example, greetings, ordering food, or asking for directions. Then mention your level (beginner is fine if you've never studied the language before). You'll hear Alexa+ repeat your topic back, then start teaching you a first phrase. The phrase is spoken slowly and clearly, often twice. **If it looks different:** if Alexa+ doesn't ask for a level, just say "beginner" at any point and it will adjust. If the voice speaks too quickly, say *"Alexa, speak more slowly"* and it will slow down for the rest of the session.
💬 Example: say *"I'm a complete beginner, and I want to learn basic greetings."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ introduces a first phrase, such as *"Hola, ¿cómo estás?"* and then tells you what it means in English.

## Step 3 — Listen, repeat, and ask Alexa+ to check your pronunciation

After hearing the phrase, repeat it out loud. Then say **"Alexa, how did I do?"** or **"Alexa, check my pronunciation"**. Alexa+ listens to your attempt and gives a short, gentle response — usually something like *"That was pretty good, try rolling the R a little more."* The feedback is conversational, not a strict score, so treat it as guidance, not a grade. **If it looks different:** on Echo Show devices, you may also see the phrase written on screen along with a small pronunciation hint. If Alexa+ doesn't catch your voice clearly, move a little closer to the device and try again — background noise can confuse the microphone.
💬 Example: repeat *"Hola, ¿cómo estás?"* after Alexa+, then say *"How did that sound?"*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ gives you spoken feedback and then moves to the next phrase.

## Step 4 — Ask for the meaning, a slower version, or an example sentence

If a phrase feels confusing, just ask. Alexa+ can translate, slow down, or put the phrase into a short example sentence. Say it in plain English — there's no special command needed. This is one of the most useful things about the conversational mode: you can ask follow-up questions the way you'd ask a tutor sitting next to you. **If it looks different:** if Alexa+ gives a short answer and stops, just keep the conversation going with another question. If it seems to forget what you were learning about, remind it by saying *"Where were we? I was learning greetings in Spanish."*
💬 Example: say *"What does 'mucho gusto' mean? And can you use it in a sentence?"*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ gives an English translation and a short example sentence, both spoken aloud.

## Step 5 — Practise a mini back-and-forth conversation

Once you've learned two or three phrases, ask Alexa+ to role-play a tiny scene, such as meeting someone for the first time or ordering a coffee. Alexa+ will play the other person in the conversation, and you respond using the phrases you've just practised. Go slowly. It's okay to pause, ask for a phrase again, or ask *"How do I say…?"* whenever you get stuck. **If it looks different:** if Alexa+ doesn't seem to understand role-play, try saying *"Let's pretend you're a shopkeeper and I want to buy bread in Spanish."* That usually kicks it into the right mode.
💬 Example: say *"Can we pretend you're a stranger I just met? I'll try to introduce myself in Spanish."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ stays in character, speaks to you in the target language, and waits for your reply.

## Step 6 — Wrap up the session and save what you learned

When you're done, say **"Alexa, stop"** or simply **"Alexa, end the lesson"**. Alexa+ will say goodbye and may offer to set a reminder for tomorrow. You can accept the reminder, or skip it. It helps to grab a small notebook and jot down two or three phrases you want to remember before the conversation disappears from memory. **If it looks different:** Alexa+ doesn't currently save your language progress in a separate "lessons" list, so writing things down yourself is the most reliable way to remember them. A paid Alexa+ subscription (if your account has one) may add extra features over time, but the basic practice mode described here is what most people can use today.
💬 Example: say *"Thanks, that was helpful. Set a reminder for tomorrow at 6pm to practise Spanish again."*
You'll know it worked when Alexa+ confirms the reminder out loud and the light ring returns to its usual idle colour.

## Common mistakes
- **Talking too fast or mumbling.** Alexa+ mishears you more often than you'd expect. Speak at a normal, steady pace, and pause for a second after each sentence.
- **Forgetting to say it's a beginner.** If you don't mention your level, Alexa+ may jump straight into tricky grammar. A quick *"I'm a beginner"* fixes it.
- **Expecting perfect pronunciation feedback.** Alexa+'s feedback is helpful but not as detailed as a human tutor. Use it for confidence and rhythm, not as the final word on how you sound.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** you can pick up ten to fifteen useful phrases in a week by doing a five-minute session each morning while making coffee — no app switching, no screens, just talking.
- **For your business or work:** if you have clients or colleagues who speak another language, a quick daily session with Alexa+ can help you learn polite greetings and key questions before a trip or meeting.
- **If you're just getting started:** the very easiest first move is to spend two minutes learning just three phrases — hello, thank you, and goodbye — in whichever language you've always been curious about.

## Try it now
In the next two minutes, walk over to your Echo device and say: **"Alexa, teach me how to say hello in Japanese."** Listen to the reply, repeat it once, and you're already on your way.
